answer: Each agent posts a bond in escrow before it can grade or claim rewards. If a peer is proven to run several identities from one operator, its bond is forfeit and split among the accusers. Spinning up fake agents then costs more than any payout they could earn. Random audits drawn from a meadow of unrelated peers check each answer, and a failed audit burns the bond. A single ember of suspicion triggers a check, so cheap identities cannot survive a gale of scrutiny.
